mcqs.question: Increasing a convolution layer's stride from 1 to 2 has what effect on its output size, holding kernel size and padding fixed?
options: The output size stays exactly the same
The output size roughly halves, since the kernel skips more positions
Stride has no relationship to output size
mcqs.explanation: Stride controls how many pixels the kernel moves between computations; a stride of 2 means the kernel visits roughly half as many positions as stride 1, shrinking the output map correspondingly. Padding and kernel size affect output size too, but stride's effect specifically is to skip positions.

mcqs.question: What specifically does parameter sharing in a convolution layer enforce?
options: Every pixel gets its own independent set of weights
The network cannot learn more than one filter per layer
Different color channels must use identical filters
The same kernel weights are reused at every spatial position, so a learned pattern detector applies uniformly across the image
mcqs.explanation: Parameter sharing means the identical kernel weights slide across every position, which is exactly what gives translation invariance and keeps the parameter count independent of image size. A CNN layer typically learns many filters, not just one, and channels aren't forced to share weights with each other.

mcqs.question: A plain (non-residual) 100-layer CNN trains worse than its 20-layer version on the same task, even on training accuracy. What's the most likely explanation?
options: Vanishing gradients across so many layers prevent early layers from learning effectively
The 100-layer model is simply overfitting the training set
The 100-layer model has too few parameters
This can never happen — deeper always means at least as good training accuracy
mcqs.explanation: Since even training accuracy is worse, this isn't an overfitting story — it's the classic degradation problem from vanishing gradients in very deep plain networks, which skip (residual) connections were specifically designed to fix. A 100-layer network has far more parameters than a 20-layer one, not fewer.
